pages.title: Cap'n Web RPC Contract
pages.purpose: The client-server and worker-worker RPC plumbing: the PublicApi/AuthenticatedApi/Overseer interfaces in api.ts, the gatekeeper contracts in gatekeeper.ts, promise pipelining, and the validator.
instructions: Document gatekeeper.ts interfaces: Vendor/User/ConnectCallback/ApprovalQueue/ObservationAuthorizer/Gatekeeper/Session.
Document the capnweb conventions: promise pipelining, RpcTarget/RpcStub, stub disposal, @validateRpc, WebSocket+RPC session.
List the three top-level RPC surfaces (PublicApi, AuthenticatedApi, Overseer) and their responsibilities.

pages.title: The Workshop Frontend SPA
pages.purpose: The packages/workshop-frontend single-page app: bootstrap, RPC connection, routing, sandboxed gadget iframes, gatekeeper app hosting, and state management.
instructions: Describe the SPA bootstrap, auth flows (password, gatekeeper sign-in, Cloudflare Access), and the WebSocket RPC session.
Describe the main pages/views: Home, Connections, Blueprints, Outputs, Settings, Admin, Chat.
Describe the sandboxed iframe model for gadgets and gatekeeper UIs (postMessage), and srcDoc frames with origin null.

pages.title: Gatekeepers & the Approval Model
pages.purpose: How gatekeepers wrap external services: three-tier hierarchy, connect flows, OAuth, approvals/simulation/observers, auto-provisioning singletons, and the MCP family.
instructions: Cover the mcp-shared trust tiers (byo/vetted), tools.ts trust boundary, and the two MCP connectors.
Document the ApprovalQueue model: submitAction/applyAction/rejectAction/revertAction, authorizeObservation, simulation, and observer verification strategies.
Explain auto-provisioned singletons and management UIs via createAccount and AccountDescription.singleton/providesUi; the three provisioning modes defined in provisioning-policy.ts.
Explain the connect flow (connectAccount/complete/callback, reconnect, ensureResources), the nonce security requirement, and the gatekeeper-google reference.

pages.title: The Workshop Backend (Kernel)
pages.purpose: Deep dive into packages/workshop-backend: entrypoints, Durable Objects, user/overseer data flow, admin settings, blueprint storage, AI invocation, and the security chokepoints.
instructions: Describe the three Durable Object classes (UserDurableObject, OverseerDurableObject, AdminSettings) and their responsibilities and relationships.
Explain the agent (overseer) and code-mode harness, bindings/env, and how the ApprovalQueue ties in.
Explain the security chokepoints: getGatekeeperClassFor in user.ts, readAdminConfig, #isAdmin in server.ts, env-var-driven auth config.
Explain workspace lifecycle, provisional gadgets, share keys, and collaborations briefly.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Top-level map of the system: the OS analogy, the kernel/backend, frontend SPA, router, gatekeepers, shared RPC contracts, and how they connect.
instructions: Describe the three-tier gatekeeper hierarchy (Vendor/User/Instance) and the capability-based security model.
Explain the kernel/devices/shell/processes OS analogy from README and connect each piece to a real package.
Explain the routing model: router is the public origin, routes /api and /gatekeeper/* by GATEKEEPER_ binding scan.

pages.title: Build, Test, and Lint Workflows
pages.purpose: The Vite+/vp toolchain: cached tasks, per-package builds, the env-stripping rules, vite-plus caching pitfalls, and how the test tasks work.
instructions: Document lint: oxlint via vp, correctness+suspicious as errors, unused-var rules, no type-aware rules yet, tsgo as tsc.
Document the env-stripping of cached vp runs first, then the FORMAT_BLUEPRINTS_DIR and workspace path caveats.
Document the per-package test task, with-timeout watchdog, workerd pool assert, and the singleThreaded tsconfig decision.
Explain pnpm build / pnpm test / pnpm lint and the difference between a script and a task (vite-plus).

pages.title: Change Guide: Adding a New Gatekeeper
pages.purpose: A focused, representative maintenance task: the full workflow to author, wire up, and ship a new gatekeeper package, including the review bar.
instructions: Cover the configurator-ui build path, types.txt symlink, GatekeeperVendor binding, registration in wrangler.jsonc, and self-destruct alarm.
Refer to the review bar: gatekeepers aren't the kernel but still must hold the capability-security and observer bars.

Walk the two-phase path: Phase 1 core (vendor/user/instance, types.d.ts, connect flow, resource configurator, register binding), STOP for review; Phase 2 approval logging, caching, simulation, observers.

pages.title: Change Guide: MCP & Share-Sensitive Services
pages.purpose: A representative security-focused maintenance task: working inside packages/mcp-shared and packages/gatekeeper-cloudflare, where trust boundaries and scopes fail closed.
instructions: Explain the cloudflare gatekeeper observability layering and fail-closed scopes, worker-scoped filter re-checking, and audit logging of numeric codes only.
Explain the mcp-shared trust boundary (tools.ts) and byo/vetted tiers, the need for sdkFetch, and the queued-action store.
Give a representative change: e.g., adding a new tool resource type to mcp-shared or a new telemetry query to the cloudflare observability session.

pages.title: Release Pipeline
pages.purpose: How customer instances are deployed and updated: the scripts/release flow, byte-identical builds, the manifest, R2 upload/promote, and the deploy wizard inputs.
instructions: Describe build-release, upload-release (candidate), promote-release; the manifest contract and golden-file test; NO_DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS; deploy-inputs.json.
Explain the placeholders ($ACCOUNT_ID, $WORKER_NAME, etc.) and that backend instance-state vars are injected at PUT time, never manifest-templated.

pages.title: Cloudflare OS Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: how to run, build, test, lint, and safely change the repository, and how to start developing a new gatekeeper.
instructions: Cover the local run paths (pnpm run-local, pnpm dev-server + pnpm dev-client), how to build/type-check with pnpm build, run tests (pnpm test, per-package test:run vs vp run), and lint with pnpm lint.

Include the minimum repo conventions every change must respect: pnpm not npm, RPC promise pipelining, RPC stub disposal, @validateRpc, logger usage, env-var auth config vs AdminConfig, singleThreaded tsconfig, no baseUrl.
Point to the gatekeeper-to-add flow as a representative first change, referencing the write-gatekeeper skill and gatekeeper.ts canonical interface file.
